An American woman has been jailed for 18 months after being found guilty of raping a four-year-old boy on her way back from school in northern Ireland.

Jennifer Breen, who was 25 at the time of the attack, pleaded guilty to four counts of rape and one count each of indecent assault and making indecent photographs of a child – all of which she carried out on April 30, 2010.

The attack took place in Ballygawley, County Down, the day after Breen had been admitted to prison for carrying a knife. The court heard that one of her victims had been playing outside the school gates while Breen was driving, when she attacked him with a 'small, hard knife.'

Breen's attack came at the end of a school day when she had been released from prison where she had served 12 months for throwing a brick through a window in her home in Northern Ireland.

The court heard the boy was sitting on a curb in the street, on his way home from school, when his father said he saw Breen with the knife in her hand, the Northern News reports.

The court heard that after he shouted at Breen to stop, she stopped in her car. He then saw the child lying on the ground, bleeding from the injuries and told his family to call an ambulance.

When staff at Glenfada Hospital arrived, their first thought was to keep the boy alive until the ambulance arrived. When the paramedics arrived, Breen was screaming and trying to get away while her eyes rolled back in her head.

Breen admitted the assault on the child. The court heard that she was on medication to treat depression at the time of the offence.

A prosecution medical report said: 'The boy was conscious and alert. His lips were slightly blue and he was unresponsive with his eyes closed. His pupils were slightly dilated. His blood alcohol level was .064. I noted an absence of any bruises.'

Breen admitted six counts of rape against a five-year-old girl and one count each of indecent assault on a 10-year-old boy and a four-year-old boy.

She was originally sentenced to six years in prison with the final year suspended and a curfew of 6pm to 6am.

But after Breen refused to leave jail when remanded in custody, Crown Judge Peter Smith jailed her for 18 months.

A team of archaeologists from the United States and Israel have found evidence of a settlement dating back some 4,000 years, in what is believed to be the most important early farming town in the world.

The new finding appears in the journal Antiquity: Archaeological Exploration.

"This is a unique find. The town was not built after the Neolithic Revolution. It's the very earliest city we know of," said Prof. Yosef Garfinkel, Director of the Institute of Hebrew Scriptures and Ancient Near Eastern Civilizations at University, who led the expedition.

A team of about 300 researchers from universities in the US and Israel found evidence of five cities that were not only used for farming and manufacturing but also contained a water supply for growing vegetables and millets, with water that was pumped from wells on the outskirts of the settlements. The most likely origin of the wells is the Neolithic Revolution, from about 8,000 BC to 2,500 BC.

Based on the discovery of an ancient road, the researchers believe the town of Tell Haris was at its biggest when the road was laid. However, the water sources near the settlement, as well as archaeological finds in the archaeological park at the site, suggest the town was a bustling city before the roads of Tell Haris were built.

The ancient site of Tell Haris is located on the Syrian border close to the Yarmouk Valley, the last historic place of the first Jewish city on the continent. This was where some 1,500 Jews lived before they were destroyed by the Muslim invading armies in 612 AD. As there are few finds from the first 300 years after the city was destroyed, the evidence that has been found indicates that there were communities in the region up to 4,000 years ago.

According to Garfinkel, the earliest evidence of the settlement of Tell Haris is dated between 4,000 and 3,500 years ago when there was agriculture on the site.

The new finds confirm that the settlement existed up to this period, suggesting that there was a larger group of people living in the region and that people probably left the area between 3,000 BC and 4,000 BC for the region of modern Lebanon.

The archaeological investigations were carried out in cooperation with the Palestinian Authority. For the first time, the team was able to see the remains of the buildings and ancient terraces in the northern area of the Tell Haris settlement.

On a chilly Wednesday night, at an upscale restaurant in Westfield, a few dozen people ate dinner in hushed, somber silence, and one woman spoke in a clear, confident voice about a subject that is the subject of considerable debate in Cincinnati: marijuana use.

"Marijuana has changed my life," said Karen Armstrong, 62, of West Price Hill, a physician, who started using marijuana when she was in her mid-50s.

Her topic was part of a discussion about marijuana legalization at the group's meeting at the New Hill Tavern, and the room felt somewhat more relaxed than it would have had, say, the topic been a discussion about breast cancer.

"It wasn't about breast cancer," she said, "but it could be."

Armstrong has been a longtime advocate of allowing medical conditions, like arthritis and pain, to be treated with the same drugs as the rest of us without fear of arrest. She said at the time when she began using marijuana that she used it for back pains and headaches, and for relief from her migraines. It has helped her sleep at night, and it helped her deal with her stress and anxiety.

She described her experience of using marijuana as "a positive moment," adding that she's never tried it to get high, just to "take it slow to see what happens."

"Now my job is more social — it's more of a support role (to marijuana proponents) than any other role," she said. She said she understands that "pot can change you," but it's a drug of great value to so many people for medical reasons.

More: Marijuana group is pushing to make Cincinnati a medical marijuana state

More: Cincinnati City Council to consider marijuana legalization ordinance

Armstrong has been an active member of the group, called Parents for Medical Marijuana, though she isn't an organizer. She was at the meeting Thursday and the other night, and spoke briefly after a series of speakers talked about the benefits of the marijuana plant, and the need to reduce the number of opioid prescriptions being written in this country.

As for the other group she's a part of, Patients Out of Time, Armstrong said it doesn't condone marijuana use, and she doesn't feel it should be legalized.

"It's a hard pill to swallow" she said, adding, "It's a bad idea, it's not worth it, it's not healthy, it's not safe."

She's also not a "stoner," a term used online by people who use marijuana as a recreational form of recreation. Marijuana is now legal for adults in six states — Alaska, Colorado, Oregon, Washington, D.C. and the District of Columbia — and 11 states have some type of decriminalized or legalized pot, which can be prescribed for medical purposes. Some cities have passed laws allowing for the sale of pot cigarettes, in some cases to residents over 21 years old with a medical marijuana card.

In March, voters in Nevada approved a ballot measure that would allow people to use medical marijuana for some medical conditions.

If medical marijuana becomes legal in Cincinnati — Armstrong would support that — it will mean that it won't be illegal for anyone, and it will allow more access to the plant for qualified patients.

Armstrong said she hopes the federal government would consider removing marijuana from its list of Schedule One drugs, which is reserved for the most dangerous drugs that have no medical value.

"That would be really good for me, for my patients, but to be honest, I'd probably still be using it if Schedule Two was still on the book, because I'm concerned about the lack of research," she said.

More: Ohio doctor files lawsuit against doctor-prescribed medical-marijuana

Armstrong said at the beginning that it was hard for her, but then she asked her husband, who is also a physician, what he would do if marijuana becomes legal in his state.

He laughed and said he'd have to get on his knees and pray.

The number of migrants arriving in Italy is set to surge to almost 1.5 million this year as European countries and the EU struggle to cope with the worst migrant crisis since World War II.

Italy's interior ministry announced the new tally on Monday, as EU interior ministers met in Brussels to discuss ways to respond to the crisis.

This year's refugee influx, which has seen 1,848 people drown or go missing since the start of the year, has exacerbated tensions over migration across the Continent.

As many as 300,000 people fleeing wars in Syria, Afghanistan, Eritrea, Nigeria and Iraq are arriving on Italy's shores, with many crossing illegally from North Africa to Sicily.

The United Nations' refugee agency (UNHCR) has said the surge has become even more difficult to handle due to the deterioration of the situation in Libya, where European governments have offered aid to the authorities fighting back an Islamic State advance.

The European Commission earlier this month said it was set to give Italy some €250 million (£200 million) to deal with the problem.

The country is struggling to cope with the sheer numbers of people leaving from North Africa with little regard for national laws and rules.

On Sunday, Italy's interior minister, Angelino Alfano, urged European partners to help speed up deportations and find alternative places for those whose asylum bids are rejected in the EU member state.

Many asylum seekers have taken the dangerous journey across the Mediterranean to Italy, where they hope to seek new lives in Europe.

But a growing number of European governments are concerned that as many as 800,000 migrants will need to be relocated by September to cope with a further flow of refugee arrivals.

The UN said in July that more people were attempting the crossing as the risk of being found and returned home was increasing.

Its purpose was to try to ensure that Germany would not be left to shoulder the brunt of the burden.

The group comprises three representatives from Germany's three main parties — Social Democrats (SPD), Greens and Left party — as well as the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV).

There is no clear plan yet on how the groups plan to work together. They will meet next week to determine which other ministers from other member states they will meet.

Germany is a major destination for migrants, and Chancellor Angela Merkel has spoken of her fear of turning over a new leaf with her country's European neighbours after it took in 1.1 million asylum seekers last year.

Postal revenue, driven by Postal Service First Class mail, fell 7.0 percent. First Class mail had shrunk by 4 percent compared with a year ago, due partly at least in part to last week's news that the Postal Service will raise its prices for first-class mail by 7 percent starting July 1. Revenue from First Class sales rose 1.5 percent compared with the year prior.

The Postal Service also lowered its guidance for 2012. The agency anticipated revenues of $44.2 billion for the year, down from its previous projection of $45.3 billion. In addition, the Postal Service now expects first-class letter and package mail to drop by 16 percent and 14 percent, respectively, in 2012 than in the prior year, which the Postal Service projects will bring in $15.7 billion in revenue.

The Postal Service is cutting 22,000 positions by the end of the year in response to a looming $5.5 billion pension liability as the agency nears a projected loss of $15 billion in future years.

The Postmaster General, Patrick Donahoe, blamed the Postal Service's financial problems on Congress's inability to pass comprehensive postal reform in the 2012 session of Congress. "The Postal Service is in a downward spiral, driven by a chronic inability to raise revenue and maintain services without jeopardizing the financial future of the nation's largest private-sector employer," he wrote in a letter to members of Congress.

The Postal Service has been under pressure from Capitol Hill to stop collecting on its $80 billion in unfunded retiree healthcare obligations. On Thursday, Donahoe told the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, "I am concerned not just about the future of the Postal Service, but that of the entire U.S. Postal Service family."

During a hearing Wednesday, the committee's Democrats argued that it's "unfair to ask all of those responsible for the service of the American people to cover the costs of our nation without compensation for those efforts," noting that a postal worker must buy postage and a letter is an asset. A congressional aide, speaking on condition of anonymity, told the Associated Press that the White House will ask Congress to take over the Postal Service.

The Postal Service is an agency under the jurisdiction of the Postal Regulatory Commission, which was created by Congress in the late 1990s to ensure that the Postal Service operates at arm's length from political pressures. The Postal Service was one of only four agencies with this kind of oversight.

There are four main unions representing postal workers. The American Postal Workers Union, the National Association of Letter Carriers and the National Postal Mail Handlers Association have all endorsed Democratic presidential candidates.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has launched the Global Plan to Reduce and Control Air Pollution to help save lives.

According to the WHO's Global Pollutant Reductions Targets (GPRTs), as many as 10 million deaths are attributed to air pollution each year. Around 1.3% of the world's population – between 668 million and 1 billion people – live in areas that experience extremely high levels of air pollution. China in particular has the highest number of people killed by air pollution with the highest rate of pollution in the world. In terms of the population in poor districts, about 18% of the world's population live in areas that experience extremely high levels of air pollution. The number for the United States is about 6%.

WHO describes air pollution as "an ever present and significant threat to public health" and calls it the #2 health risk in the world. For an individual, it can lead to respiratory troubles such as asthma, bronchitis, heart disease and stroke, as well as cause chronic and acute diseases such as cardiorespiratory disease, asthma, bronchitis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), among others.

Among some of the measures to reduce air pollution in China is to introduce new regulations on heavy vehicles, especially large SUVs and big trucks.

WHO and its partners also plan to accelerate the implementation of the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and Global Plan on Tobacco Control to combat tobacco use and improve the quality of health as well as reduce the burden of smoking-related diseases.

"We're launching a Global Plan to Reduce and Control Air Pollution because we know that we've got to tackle pollution if we're to reduce air pollution and save lives. For this to work, we need a long-term global strategy, and more than ever, we need to be working together. We have the capacity and capability to act, and we know the ways in which we can help. It's in our hands. All we ask is for everyone to give their best effort," said Dr Flavia Bustreo, Director of WHO's Department of Environmental Health.

The plan involves tackling five key areas: 1. Prevention through increased availability of clean fuels, alternative fuels, cleaner vehicles, cleaner fuels and emissions reduction from the economy, 2. Prevention through improved access to clean cooking and heating fuels, clean fuels for cooking and heating, better building regulation and improved building energy efficiency, 3. Prevention through improved access to adequate and affordable public transport, including public transport for the elderly and disabled, affordable public transport for the poor, and improved public transport, 4. Prevention and control of air pollution by addressing sources of air pollution and its transport, the environment and the economy, including waste of fresh water and other human activities and pollution from the environment, 5. The promotion of the implementation of air pollution policies internationally and implementation of relevant national air pollution policies.

The New York Times recently reported that Google is building a system to "keep track of which links you click and how often they're repeated". They say this will "improve your own and your users' experience while helping Google do better at detecting spam, malware and extremist sites".

A recent example shows how this may work. If you have a Google search term 'how is the weather in New York', you get this list of related results:

I clicked on each link, which led me to this article on Weather Underground.

I then clicked on one link to the top of the list, which led me straight to this article on The Wall Street Journal. That's a very different experience than I'd have seen if I had clicked on the first link in the list. So perhaps Google's new system can improve my experience and reduce the number of searches from me to people who are not interested in these sorts of posts. (Not to mention the other problems with the site.)

I know that this is a bit over the top, but it's hard to imagine that Google needs to know how often I click on links and I'm not interested in that information. But it seems to me that this is a way of building up a database of user behaviours, and I am definitely not happy to have such a database to keep track of and see which types of content have been given more than they deserve and which haven't. I can certainly understand why Google is putting this initiative into place. It will likely make their site more resilient against spam as people who have been blacklisted for their political views on political debate are less likely to click on links to websites containing such content, which will only benefit Google. I can totally see my own side of the argument as to how people find out about the content of these sites in the first place. And indeed I also understand that the reason this is in place is to improve the experience for people who are searching for content rather than for people who are trying to find content. For these reasons I am ok with Google doing this, and I will try to go without clicking on links from now on.

An international group of astronomers has found that giant black holes at the heart of galaxies rotate faster than expected and have huge amounts of magnetic fields that keep them from emitting radiation that would otherwise destroy nearby stars. In addition to these properties, the discovery of strong magnetic fields around the centers of black holes is very unusual. Scientists still don't understand how black holes grow.

While the Milky Way, the Magellanic Clouds, and many other galaxies are believed to have formed from a huge cloud of gas and dust, some of which was ripped apart by a supermassive black hole long ago, they contain stars and many galaxies contain a few million stars.

Although most of these galaxies have been studied extensively, the nature of the magnetic fields around the galactic centers has lagged behind. In the early 1980s, a team led by Peter Adler from the University of Utah at Salt Lake City hypothesized that giant black holes with a mass about five times that of our Sun (which makes them about seven times the mass of our Sun), could make a significant contribution to the development of a magnetic field around their galactic cores.

This idea was supported through theoretical work by other scientists using high-energy X-ray photons from a wide variety of sources to probe the properties of various magnetisms at the heart of black holes. Adler's group found that the magnetic fields of these black holes were highly polarized — or polarizing — compared with those in other regions.

In fact, a typical black hole had a magnetic field of about 300 Gauss: a value far beyond what was expected for such a massive body. This extreme field is known as Kerr effect because it was first predicted by the Belgian-American physicist, Dr. Hermann Kerr.

When the Kerr effect is applied to our own galaxy, the galactic center, it creates strong magnetic fields around the supermassive black hole that are about 300% stronger than what is seen around typical black holes (that is, on the scale in which the Kerr effect is seen) at the other galactic centers. The strong magnetic fields are believed to be connected to powerful magnetic fields generated by massive clouds of radiation from the black hole.

A new analysis of data from the Cosmic Assembly Near-infrared Deep Extragalactic Legacy Survey (CAII-DISCOVERY) has now determined how strong the magnetic fields are around the galactic centers of large galaxies. The team is led by Dr. G. Pasi Seuiri from the University of Hertfordshire, and included Dr. Adler, Dr. James B. Kowalski of the University of Utah, and Dr. A. F. Finkbeiner of the University of Chicago.

The magnetic field surrounding the center of a galaxy is not uniformly strong or weak and is not the same everywhere. Instead, the strong magnetic field at the centers is determined as the number of polarizations it has, i.e., the number of different magnetic orientations. The number is measured as the maximum intensity of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by a black hole, which is then used in some models to calculate the number of protons and ions in the gas of a galactic center.

According to the new research, the strong magnetic field around large galactic nuclei (which the researchers had named large-magnetospheric-field-center-galaxies) is very small, on the order of 50 Gauss with a significant difference between the centers of different large galaxies. That means that the cosmic radiation from a black hole could exert a significant influence, either through the gravitational pull (located to the left of the line) or through the strong magnetic fields surrounding them.

The researchers also found that the magnetic field around the galactic nuclei of some very large galaxies is so strong that in some cases the whole galaxy was distorted. A small variation in the magnetic strength of the galactic nuclei could cause some galaxies to move away from one another, as shown in Figure 1.

The researchers also determined the structure of the magnetic polarization. They found that the magnetic polarization in this case is not very symmetric and seems to have been shaped over tens of millions of years. However, in some cases it does not really fit the known structure of the magnetic field. The results of their analysis have been published in the journal Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

"With this paper, we can use this technique to determine how the magnetic poles have behaved over the past few billion years," said Dr. Adler, who is also the University of Chicago's John E. Baez Professor of Astronomy at the University. "The large value of the magnetic field around the galactic nuclei in Figure 1 suggests that they were formed at this time; the asymmetry in a few galactic nuclei suggests that the magnetic field at the center of the galaxy was much stronger than average. This is a surprising new twist to our theory."

According to these findings, the magnetic fields could have developed in a very different way than was previously expected,

Mozilla and a team of security researchers are working to prevent exploits from taking down websites as hackers become better at finding them and exploiting them.

In an announcement Thursday, the organization said it has released an Android app called DoSBox. The first thing the app does is analyze the attack process and identify the common and unusual parts used in most successful attacks. "It's as close as we'll ever get to an antivirus for websites," said John Lilly, an Android developer at Mozilla who was part of the attack prevention team that invented DoSBox.

DoSBox is part of the Firefox Security Project, a global community working to enhance the security of Web browsers. Firefox itself is the number-two user, after Google, of Android.

DoSBox can identify and block most attacks without resorting to complex code. "It's good at being more simplistic than that," Lilly said, adding that the app can block malicious URL and browser cookies based on their path.

The Firefox Security Project is "probably the most ambitious work on websites security," said David Manger, a senior security evangelist with Mozilla.

The effort will help keep mobile attacks down and enable "a set of security controls for people using browsers that they use themselves, so browsers are secure for their users," he said. One of those controls, he said, has been the security cookie, a common piece of software that allows a malicious Web page to install itself on a user's browser. Cookies can allow a malicious site to collect data about the user's browsing habits and to exploit other vulnerabilities in the browser.

Mozilla added that DoSBox is an extension of a separate project it has used and is using. The group called Censorspy monitors the Web to detect malicious URL manipulation or tampering.

The Firefox Security Project is being developed by Firefox developer Martin Schmale, Lilly and a dozen other security experts. Mozilla is encouraging other vendors and other partners to participate as well.

Among them is Google, which contributed to the effort, as Mozilla is doing on the Android app. Google declined to comment.

China has issued new guidelines for pollution in its major coastal cities, ahead of a three-day summit meeting being hosted by Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe.

The Ministry of Environmental Protection's air quality report says the capital, Beijing, is not eligible for special pollution-reduction measures under rules set by the World Bank.

It says cities like Shanghai and Tianjin are eligible for the restrictions.

Abe will also discuss with Chinese President Xi Jinping a new declaration for climate change.

"Japan is a strong supporter of China's environment development. We will talk about a new global climate change treaty that strengthens cooperation between the world's two leaders," Mr Abe later told a news conference in Beijing.

"We are determined in our efforts and in the determination to protect the environment."

Mr Abe also plans to discuss with Mr Abe's counterpart, Li Keqiang, a statement to mark the 50th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Xinhua news agency reports.

China's environment ministry has issued a new air quality index index for six major Chinese cities that was released to coincide with Mr Abe's visit. This is based on data from six air monitoring stations, and has been used by foreign experts for years to gauge air quality.

The news agency says that from Saturday (3 August) Beijing will be considered to be "good" for its air quality. That is one notch above hazardous, and the levels of PM2.5 - tiny air particulates that can penetrate deeply into the lungs - of PM2.5 in the capital now are below those in central cities.

'Huge concerns'

Earlier this month, Mr Abe said he had agreed to "conclude discussions" on a document to mark the centenary of the People's Republic of China.

The story is a bit complicated, but a few weeks back, our readers were treated to the story that Google (GOOG) was working on a Google Glass-style eyewear that is meant for use in public places like trains and planes. While the product may have been in the works years before this report, it looks like at least some of the tech giant's engineers are working on the devices.

I'm not exactly sure how far along the "Glass experience" is on the product side, but I know that a couple of my friends at Business Insider have one themselves, and I've been seeing a lot of other photos of what look to be prototype (i.e., "work-in-progress") Glass-like devices, like ones that look something like eyeglasses. My friends have also reported hearing buzz in public places while wearing Google Glass, but I've also been hearing reports from friends of people wearing the Glass in restaurants, bars, casinos or the like so far.

A lot of the speculation has focused on the fact that the Glasses may include a built-in camera and some form of voice control, but it would seem likely that those parts of the device will be built into larger glasses that can be worn on the same frame as Google Glass.

I also heard reports from people in other parts of the tech world who wear some or all of the Google Glass prototype at various points in their lives, and some of these people are pretty excited about the product. This news brings a little greater clarity to what I wrote about a month ago:

A Google Glass experience is something that, even if you're not wearing it, you'll get every time you're around people who do wear it. Google Glasses can make the "unplugged" part of a daily commute into an experience that you'll have every single day.

The problem with this scenario is that the product does not come to us until sometime in 2015, and we're likely not going to experience it until at least the end of the year. The most obvious reason Google Glass may not ship by the end of the year is because it's too expensive ($1,500 for the first version) for too few people to buy one.

So, is Google really going to market this product in 2015? I don't think it's entirely out of the question. It's a long-lived product after all, and one that they have spent a number of years building, and they may just be trying to move the product ahead of schedule. Or maybe it's something more, I'm not really sure.

What I do know is that it looks like Google is making a concerted effort to get Glass into the public, and that some parts of the process could be quite disruptive.

How do you know if that one's going to fall right to you? It's the magic of sound. When the human body registers that sound from another, its heart rate quickens and breathing gets more rapid, indicating that it's headed right for you. For humans, the exact position you'll be struck by a bullet is determined by the sound of its firing and the angle at which it lands.

And if you're a bullet, if they see that your chest is flat like a target, they don't have to hit you. Your body is so sensitive to sound that, in one experiment, participants' hearts jumped if they heard a bullet coming at them from two feet away, and even as loud as 150 decibels, or about as loud as a jackhammer if you are really close, and their pupils dilated.

"When our ears hear sound, we don't see it; we don't know what it is," says Philip Fosse, a professor of physical chemistry and professor of anatomy at Emory University in Atlanta. But our minds do.

Sound can help us predict how close a bullet will be to us by triggering our body's response to danger. "If you want to shoot a gun, your brain says you might be in danger, so you have to be in position," says Daphne Merckx, head of the neuroscience program at the National Federation of Bullet Collectors, which has about 200 members, out of a population between 12,000 and 14,000. "And we have different organs in our body that detect sound differently. One is our blood vessels. When you look at the surface of the wall of the vessel, it is different from when you look at the back where your veins are."

"It's not as obvious, but there is blood vessels all over the face of the body," says Merckx. "They react very differently from blood vessels in the chest. If you shoot with a rifle, and you see that your face is white, that means you are in danger, and your eyes will go big. You will start turning around, and you will try to figure it out. But if you shoot by ear, and your eyeballs go back and you see that you are not in danger, you will not try to figure it out. You are not as affected."

She says she doesn't know the name for those different systems that are involved in responding to a threat. "But it's an important one since one person could hear a burst or sound, and another would not."

Fosse and his colleagues created an artificial auditory environment in which an actor played a single shot, then the same shooting location was recreated five times. "The actor said she was standing behind her partner, and she started to shoot at him," says Fosse. "We then played back five different shots in five different scenarios. Each one got the blood vessel response at 60 decibels, which corresponds to the sound of gunfire. Our hypothesis was that people who were standing in front of and behind the partner and had heard gunshots would think that they were in danger and that would cause their blood vessels to react."

When they tested the accuracy of their predictions, the scientists could tell from the movement of the actor's face that she was in danger and trigger the blood vessels for blood flow. They then recorded where the bullet struck, with the accuracy of their predictions, on the body. Then they tested the accuracy of the blood vessel response with new gunshots. When the actor said the bullet was in the direction of her partner, the blood vessels closed because they sensed danger. In the opposite scenario, when the bullet was in the direction of the actor, the vessels did not react.

The more accurate of their predictions was the one on which the actor reacted the most quickly. The results are published in PNAS.

Even if the person is not wearing any protection, their heartbeat raises their blood pressure, and that can cause temporary blindness in some people. But blood vessels don't close immediately, says Merckx. "You do not have the first heartbeat, so if you don't see the blood vessels open, it's very difficult to know that your heart isn't stopping. But you do see the pupil dilated. We know when it does."

But even one second of not seeing a bullet for a split second is enough to set off a response from those little vessels that say, hey, there's something in danger.

"You can't predict it, but by your peripheral vision, the blood vessels in your face know to stop the heart," says Merckx. Cream cheese filling

Here's what you'll need:

1/2 cup cream cheese (softened, room temperature)

1/4 cup powdered sugar (I used white)

1 egg

1 teaspoon vanilla extract

1 cup white sugar

In a large bowl, beat cream cheese with powdered sugar until well blended, but not completely smooth. Add the egg, vanilla, and 1 cup of white sugar and mix to form a "cookie dough" consistency. Press 3-4 tablespoons of cookie dough onto parchment lined cookie sheets.

Bake for 8 minutes at 350 degrees, until top is set but still soft. Cool for 3 minutes, then chill until set (about 8 to 10 hours), or refrigerate. Mozilla has released a new version of the Firefox web browser to address vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution.

The new version, version 46.0.2357.111, addresses several vulnerabilities, including one that could allow an attacker to steal a victim's account password. Mozilla also addressed some memory safety issues.

In a statement given at the Black Hat USA tech conference in Las Vegas on Friday, Mozilla security researcher Will Thompson said that the fixes "include additional mitigations to address a memory safety issue, some additional logic that is being reviewed and will be addressed."

"Further vulnerabilities will be added if and when appropriate," he added.

In his talk, Thompson stressed that the latest version is the fifth major release of the browser. In March, it received version 47, which fixed a bug that could have caused the browser to crash, and included Firefox Aurora, an update that added features for mobile and tablet users and Firefox for Linux.

Mozilla has not yet fixed another flaw that could allow an attacker to inject ads into Web content, which may have been another security vulnerability that attracted the attention of researchers in the wake of recent high profile hacks. Thompson said at that time that Mozilla had closed the security hole.

Security researchers have long been urging Mozilla to address bugs that could cause remote code execution vulnerabilities. In July, it disclosed an exploit for one such vulnerability in Firefox that affected many Web servers, which could have allowed an attacker to compromise a server.

The Web browser market is highly competitive, and Firefox users tend not to switch to other browsers anytime soon, because Firefox is free and Mozilla offers support and security updates.

The latest release also marks the end of the stable development cycle for Firefox, at least for now. Thompson said that his next priority is to "start working on other security issues."

Thompson's talk and the announcement could be read as an attempt to gain some legitimacy for the company's efforts.

Firefox users are encouraged to update their software by installing a Mozilla security update in the next 24 hours. The update will include a vulnerability notice for any remaining bugs that remain after the release of the new version.

Mozilla said in its statement that its work with security researchers continues. A spokesperson said that such activity will include efforts to "continue to address security vulnerabilities in other products."

The problem? If our high school teachers are anything to go by, those in college are ready and willing to use their platform to get some fun facts on the subject.

First up is this tweet, sent by someone using the handle @NickyWantsToParty, which claims to show what a high school girl's response would be to her wearing a mini skirt. (It should be noted here that if someone on the Internet is wearing any kind of skirt or pantyhose, they can almost certainly expect to be mocked for not wearing shorts. Just ask the students at West Virginia.)

For those of you who find this amusing, I apologize. You get the joke but I'm sure there were probably some decent responses in this scenario — as well as ones that would be funny in any situation — that I'm missing. Here are my two cents:

1. Some people think it's fine to say "you look like an adult," and expect them to respond in kind. That happens to me all the time. I get it, you're wearing a skirt. That's why it's not "adult." But when you start saying things that are actually derogatory, it's time to call it out. It's not fun to tell jokes about women like this. And let's face it, if you're a teacher and want to say "you look like an adult," it certainly won't get a laugh from someone sitting in a classroom and expecting that everyone in the class would just sit by and take it.

2. Another common problem I've seen: A group of guys are sitting in a group conversation and one says "she looks like a fucking schoolgirl." There's nothing offensive about that statement, but the fact that a teacher would do it makes it seem like a sexist comment and sends the message that any teacher can say anything they want about that particular student.

You can see what I'm getting at, right? You shouldn't say such things, and you shouldn't let people say such things in an effort to make your "adult" comment seem more "adult."

And, lastly, I want to mention a couple of other things that were said about this particular student. When the student showed up for class she received a lot of "why don't you look more professional?" or "go home girl / guy" comments.

When the Internet becomes too slow to meet these demands, we will finally open up our world to the outside world; this is called a bottleneck event, and it will occur sooner rather than later.

On March 31, 2012, a man named Adam Lanza killed 26 people and wounded 17 in an elementary school in Newtown, CT. The massacre has inspired a number of books, films, and TV shows about the Newtown shooting, but its tragic legacy has largely gone untold. As a public health researcher, I've often heard people discuss the Sandy Hook Elementary School attack, and its connection to mental illness. When someone has a serious mental illness but is also in pain, a great deal of mental pain often accompanies it. In particular, people who are in pain have a greater sensitivity to their own pain, and they often try to reduce their own pain in order to alleviate others' pain.

When someone who is experiencing an immediate pain response wants to relieve their own pain, they might feel anxious about how the action might contribute to other people's pain by reducing their own. This anxiety might lead someone to choose to reduce their own pain without thinking about the unintended consequences.

When someone who is suffering from a mental health condition takes an action to relieve their other pain, they might feel a rush of adrenaline and feel strong, even though the action is likely to make their other pain worse.

But this isn't just an issue faced by the mentally ill. This is also a problem faced by millions of people who want to relieve their own pain. If someone is suffering from emotional pain and is also experiencing physical pain, this may result in their physical pain causing their emotional pain.

A study I recently conducted with my former student, Jennifer L. Riggs , revealed that people frequently act in ways that reduce their own pain when dealing with pain that they perceive as other people's. This suggests a possible explanation for the phenomenon of the "pain-less pain" effect.

How I became a feminist

It seems that since the internet became the central communication tool in the human race, there are those out in the dark corners of the Internet who are determined that they're not all-knowing. I'm not one of them. I don't have access to the dark, dark corners of the internet.

I understand that there are people who do have access to that dark corners of the internet. Many of them will look in the wrong place if you asked them for the answer to an obscure feminist question.

I don't consider the internet "the real world." I do not believe it is where human lives are made or end.

I've gotten a lot of pushback over the past few months from the feminist community. Some of it has been really mean and nasty and I haven't had any time to deal with it. Some of it has been really nice, some of it has been stupid. It's been overwhelming to deal with all of it, so I'll do my best here to try and explain the motivations behind my political views.

I grew up in a little town outside of Minneapolis on a farm. Mom and dad had both gone to school. My parents are straight, married, white. I grew up with a sense of community. In a world where your parents tell you that your color is the cause of all your problems, it's quite amazing to see that a simple farm makes a village. This wasn't a world where people were oppressed because they were different. People were oppressed because I was different.

I didn't grow up surrounded by other men. I never talked to any other girls or women of the village for that matter. I knew that there were some boys who did play around and some girls who did have relationships with other boys. I didn't grow up feeling like I was going to be bullied for being different. I didn't experience any of my teachers being sexist or homophobic. They didn't treat me differently than the boys or girls around here. My teachers were kind and accepting of girls.

At an early age I realized I couldn't escape my family's values. To an extent, it was my parents. But I realized it wasn't just my parents' values that kept me quiet and afraid.

I started to realize that it wasn't my family that was wrong. I was wrong. That was the first step toward wanting to fight for women's rights, for the right for women to be treated equally. I was wrong. I had failed to live up to my parents' ideals. I needed to be a better boy. I needed to be one that wasn't afraid of being different.

I wanted to be a boy.

But that was impossible, wasn't it?

I'm sorry. I hope that's the wrong word to use.

I did what I could. I was smart. I was good at school. I went to great colleges for college and graduate school. I took part in the student activism movement. I was involved in the women's studies movement. I took dance classes. I participated in the theater and music classes. I participated in the debate club. I participated in the debate society. What is VAC?

VAC stands for Virtual Air Traffic Control. It is a set of radio links that connects planes in a particular airspace to controllers in air-trafficking networks.

The link uses a frequency band of about 600 GHz frequencies. For this reason, the equipment does work only in specific parts of the earth's magnetic field.

In theory, the aircraft is connected to the controller by an air-traffic control radio link. In practice, the controller is also connected through an aerial network to the aircraft by a "radar-based radio link" or a radar-based radio link (RBL). The radar-based radio link works by sending data (e.g., aircraft information) to a ground radar station.

The aircraft radio link uses very low frequency ("VLF") communications, while the radar-based radio link uses very high frequency ("HF"), communications. This helps avoid interference between the radio systems and helps avoid interference between the radio networks.

In addition, VAC links use two types of links (radio links). Both link types are intended for general aviation. If the flight requires very sensitive and/or emergency communications, a VAC Link is more suitable. If the flight does not require critical communications, a VAC Link is more suitable.

What is VHF?

With VHF radio communications, aircraft have very strong interference problems with radar-based radio networks. The main cause for this problem is radar-based radio links. The radar-based radio link used in VHF is different from a "Radar-based radio link" (RBL). (See The Radar-based link vs the RBL).

Why does VHF have so much stronger interference than HF?

The VHF radio frequency spectrum has many low frequencies (below 10 kHz and below 1 kHz). Even a single aircraft can cause much more interference than a radar-based radio link (RBL) in such low frequency spectrum. This is because radar-based radio links will pass through a radio that is tuned to the desired frequency. This will cause most of the unwanted radiation to be reflected back to the aircraft, causing much more interference than the RBL.

One way to make VHF's stronger interference-free is to tune the radio to the desired frequency instead of to frequency-controlled frequency.

There is a limit to the power of VHF radio frequencies. The highest power radio band (VHF/UHF) has a bandwidth of about 30 kHz. A transmitter or receiver that is designed to operate in this band will not give you the full range of the VHF bandwidth. Therefore you have to find a way to create a narrower bandband radio link to reduce interference.

We've all seen the TV shows and movies, where the characters must find love in the next generation. While this may seem to be a more plausible scenario in the real-world, finding a match in the next generation isn't all that easy. In many cases, the people we find will never be the person of our dreams — the problem lies in figuring out how and what to say to them to make it clear that it's not something that just happened to us.

And even more frustratingly, there aren't any easy options for choosing who we'll be friends with in our next generation. There are no dating apps or websites that allow parents and children to message each other (though it's a lot easier to get people to talk to children when they're younger). The best you can do is to find a couple in your age group that you want to start going out with, while keeping your eyes out for anyone who looks the least like his or her parents.

It's been a good day for the U.K. at Nationals 2014.

For as much hype as the U.K. has for winning its first-ever World Championship, all that attention is really just an echo of the excitement that followed the 2012 Olympic victory — and a way to keep the team together during a relatively short break before Nationals. That excitement didn't last long though; just like in 2012, everyone had to get back on the pitch and focus on the event in hand.

The team was successful at Nationals, advancing to the final and knocking Stanford out for the season championship. On Sunday night, however, a disappointing loss to Washington D.C. (and a very questionable call from a Ref that got away from British Columbia) marked the end of British Columbia's season and left the team without a World Championship trophy.

That's quite the downer since the team still managed to finish in the top four of Nationals and bring home more medals than they had by themselves at their inaugural College Championships in 2012. However, British Columbia had its share of issues over the weekend and some very unfortunate events put an end to the team's National dreams.

On Sunday night, two key players for British Columbia and the entire women's team struggled.

As mentioned, Emma Gratton and Kate Fletcher both came in as key roles for the team. Gratton, the lone player who played all of her Nationals matches with a different partner or substitution partner throughout the year, came in as a 2nd seed. However, Gratton, a player who often relies on her teammates to make those pivotal games in crucial situations, was struggling and ended up getting a game late in the bracket due to a terrible final position.

Fletcher, on the other hand, had another difficult weekend. She suffered an injury late in the first game, and she did not play in the rest of the matches, ultimately finishing 9th out of 10 players. Fletcher would have a second injury on Monday, and though she was not given time to heal (a rarity for a player who is out for the entire day), it put her out of the tournament altogether.

Although both players were disappointing in their performances, they were also extremely important for their teams. Gratton led British Columbia on a 3 – 1 run and won a game against Oregon to start off the weekend. Fletcher and her team nearly pulled off an upset win over Stanford, but Stanford held them on defense long enough for Gratton and her teammates to turn around and get a 4-1 win over Washington. That loss, coupled with a loss to British Columbia, leaves the Canadian women's team with just one more win of the year.

Unfortunately for the team, the three players who were most likely to step up in the moments between those two losses have been hurt in other ways. Gratton has to miss the rest of the season, which means she will be out until after the spring season, and Fletcher is also going to miss the rest of the season — she could miss as much as the first couple of weeks of Nationals unless something changes in her situation.

This is bad news for British Columbia; it's hard to envision the rest of the season as anything better than being the first team through the gates with nothing at stake at Nats.

Luckily, there wasn't any harm done at Nationals as the team had enough time to recover, work together, and try to replace those three players. However, the weekend can't have been helpful for the team as it heads into spring, just when the team needs it the most in order to be able to keep building for next season.

We hope that Gratton recovers quickly, but Fletcher is probably a game away from needing her own surgery, so the team will definitely need her as the No. 2 for the fall. In Gratton's place, it will likely be Sarah Chmielarz or Anna Meares.

The UBCV Women's squad didn't put out the best results at Nationals though, as its four wins all came against lower ranked teams. UBCV's success at Nationals came at the expense of both British Columbia and Washington; the UBCV club started off the weekend losing just two games to Canada; the rest of the team's wins were against teams much higher up this list.

There would appear to be some underlying issues with Canadian women's UBCV performance as of late. Even though the team ended the weekend with only nine wins, only 9.5% of its games were won by teams that were not ranked No. 1.

It means that UBCV's two other regular season losses were both to the top two teams, including one to Canada, and both against teams ranked at or above No. 1.

The team was also unable to advance to the semis, despite winning four games out of six. While we could see the ups and downs of that game, the team did not end up advancing out of pool play

CAMBRIDGE, MA: (US) – This September, an asteroid, designated 2016 HO3 , will cross the orbit of Earth at a distance that is greater than the moon's and slightly farther from the sun than Earth is.

To capture this distant asteroid, the European Space Agency (ESA) teamed up with a team of space-based telescopes, which include NASA's Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) and Spitzer, on a mission called NEOWISE. This near-infrared telescope, operated by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Pasadena, CA, is located at the Lick Observatory.

NEOWISE will begin collecting data on the asteroid on April 2, 2016, using the 3.6-meter Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) in Chile. The telescope will take multiple images of the asteroid with a resolution of a few centimeters. These images will be combined to create a higher-definition photo that is the most detailed image of a near-Earth object in the near-infrared light spectrum yet delivered by a space-based observatory.

"By adding this very high-resolution infrared image to our current map of the asteroid belt, and studying its color, we learn a great deal about its physical properties, shape, and internal structure. We will also learn about its past and future interactions with the sun and other asteroids," explained Thomas Reiter, JPL program scientist for NEOWISE at the time of this press conference.

"This observation will be a major milestone for astronomers and for astronomers everywhere in the world. The asteroid is an incredible opportunity for learning more about asteroid evolution, future impact events, and the presence of water vapor, volatile compounds, and other volatile compounds on the surface of NEOWISE's target. We are looking forward to this exciting collaboration in the next few weeks," added JPL's Mark Mattson.

Asteroid 2016 HO3 will come as close to the earth as 5,600 km (3,400 mi) on September 26, 2016.

About NEOWISE

NEOWISE is an ESA-led mission to search for Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) in the Main Asteroid Belt between Mars and Jupiter. The NEOWISE instrument was developed in four years after its 2010 launch, using existing infrastructure at JPL.

NEOWISE's main purpose is to detect and characterize asteroids that cross the orbit of the Earth, with a primary focus on asteroids with orbits that intersect the Earth-Moon distance of 3,600 km (2,700 mi). NEOWISE will measure the distance between the spacecraft and an asteroid at the time it passes behind the earth in order to determine the object's orbital inclination and to determine what portion of that orbit takes it inside or outside of our solar system.

In a different part of the sky (the constellation of Cancer), NEOWISE will also take a series of photographs of the large asteroid (1.5 km or 1 mile across) Sedna moving against the background stars. This infrared image and corresponding ultraviolet image will enhance our understanding of Sedna's surface, using the infrared to map features like fractures, rims and craters. Sedna will not cross the earth's orbit, but its orbit intersect the plane of the ecliptic. This allows measurements of Sedna's surface properties to be made at the same times that NEOWISE observes.

The NEOWISE image reveals about 10% of the object's surface, with Sedna's largest features (up to 10 km wide) detected as yellow-green pixels. Sedna is thought to have formed from comet debris, and may be an interesting target in the search for habitable environments around other planets. The object is approximately one-fifth the size of Sedna, but a little more than a tenth as far from the sun.

More information

For more about the mission and to download the NEOWISE science data and images, visit: http://neowise.esa.int/ and http://spacetelescope.org/home

For more information about ESA missions, visit: http://www.esa.int/main/index.cfm?Section=Missions

A newly discovered dinosaur may hold the keys for understanding the evolution of birds, a group that today has been largely defined by a few bird-specific traits such as long bills and long legs.

A new study found that dinosaurs' long faces and teeth—as well as traits such as beak-like wings—may have played an important part in setting the stage of modern birds by helping them gain a grip on their prey when their jaws weren't equipped to tear a large carcass open.

Although all dinosaurs are known to have had a relatively short pre-cranial skeleton, birds are the only group of dinosaurs currently known to have evolved long necks. But, as shown by early specimens found in Germany, North America, and Europe, dinosaurs had another way of making their long-necked heads and large chewing teeth: they had a long, toothless beak.

"By the time birds evolved, the need for such an adaptation – with its relatively minor cost in terms of bone loss – would have been obvious," says study co-author Peter Makovicky, curator of vertebrate paleontology at the Carnegie Museum of Natural History in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

But how might dinosaurs have been able to develop such traits? A number of hypotheses have been proposed, including birds having access to foods from which dinosaurs lost large amounts of bone because of eating or not eating their prey.

A new study examined the bones of a fossilized raptor Tyrannosaurus rex discovered in Montana in 2001, which have been found to contain the remnants of the largest bones ever found in that animal – long, bony neck vertebrae. A recent investigation by Makovicky and his colleagues revealed that the vertebrae were only half as thick as other dinosaur fossils, hinting at the possibility that the dinosaur had lost a little bone mass as it grew.

"We can use these findings to reconstruct what the dinosaur's body might have looked like," Makovicky explains. "This helps us understand what the environmental pressure was for these guys to evolve these traits, in particular that beak."

According to the findings, this study of Tyrannosaurus rex's skeleton has implications for the evolution of modern birds. Because the vertebrae were only about a quarter as thick as other dinosaur fossils, the dinosaur did not need to make the extra effort to shed bone for food.

"Because tyrannosaurids were smaller than dinosaurs that evolved later, these traits were likely acquired more quickly as a result of smaller and simpler environmental pressures," Makovicky says. "So, if these traits were present in the pre-Cretaceous, these dinosaurs would have needed less time to evolve or could have survived longer."

With dinosaurs having long necks, this suggests that tyrannosaurs would likely have been better able to feed on fast-moving, agile prey. With their larger, longer necks, birds have developed an adaptation of their own, with their long, narrow beaks.

The study has limitations. It is based primarily on a relatively incomplete specimen that does not represent a full-grown tyrannosaur (the skull was not found to be as long around the eyes as in some other animals). Moreover, the team did not look at Tyrannosaurus rex at the tail and so could not fully test its flight ability. The dinosaur was killed roughly 150 million years ago so its bones are of lesser size, meaning it would be unlikely to hold up as a living model. Makovicky acknowledges that the study is a preliminary assessment from a single specimen.

The research appears in the journal PLOS ONE.

PURPOSE:

This article addresses the literature related to the relationship between dietary glycemic index (GI), glycemic load (GL), and body fatness in relation to obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease (CVD).

METHODS:

We reviewed the literature concerning the relationship between GI, GL, and body fatness in the United States.

RESULTS:

There is evidence, in both prospective and cross-sectional studies, of a negative effect of higher carbohydrates and a positive one of higher fats on obesity, insulin resistance, and CVD risk. The most consistent finding of the literature is higher risk of obesity in people with GL higher than 100 compared with those with GL lower than 55. The authors also report that the risk of diabetes is much lower in low-GI individuals compared with those with higher GI and fat intakes, and that the prevalence of diabetes in this population is significantly less than that in the general population.

CONCLUSIONS:

Glycemic index appears to be a risk factor for obesity, insulin resistance, and CVD, although additional studies are needed to determine the effect of other dietary components.

A former soldier told The Associated Press he was convicted of murder by a military court in Kuwait before undergoing the sex change and returning to active military service, and he now holds American citizenship – though he's not sure of his identity.

The soldier, whose military service ended more than 12 years ago, said he began getting hormone therapy and undergoing gender reassignment surgery in 2010. He also went by the name James in Kuwait.

A new name – James – and a new birth certificate were issued to the former soldier while he was still in the military, according to the AP, which spoke with the soldier in Kuwait this month.

The AP spoke with the soldier's former commanding officer in 2009, and he confirmed that he was the former soldier in question as well as his medical records.

The former soldier told the AP that his former commanding officer, who asked not to be identified as the situation concerned military personnel, called them about the case and said the man was no longer with the military.

The case has garnered international attention as a possible violation of international law forbidding any person from being forced to undergo gender reassignment or sex change operations, the AP report said.

The man, who was convicted for killing a Kuwaiti man, told an AP reporter, that though he had served in the marines, he had had sex-change surgery during his service, which resulted in his conviction, according to the military records in question.

He was discharged under the condition that the military would not disclose his identity or record of conviction.

The AP said the soldier's current command is looking into the case and has told him he is welcome to keep the changes in place under the current policy. They said they do not know of any policy in place prohibiting sexual-change operation for members of the military who have already undergone it.

The AP said the Kuwait Military Court issued an order that the former soldier serve a jail term for killing the Kuwaiti man in 2007 and for injuring five others.

In the beginning, you are given the opportunity to choose your gender and your class:


- Soldier (human) (male)

- Sniper (human) (female)


As you play through the game, you'll be given the option of choosing another class. You can do this twice and it's not actually required, but when you do, you'll be given the option of choosing between the Soldier, Sniper, Heavy, Medic, Recon, Pyro, and Scout.


In the first game, you're given the chance to select which class you pick, which allows you the chance to become stronger as an individual. In the sequel, you are able to become stronger only when you choose a class, but your progress will be slower in the process as a consequence.


There are three different classes to choose from.


- Soldier (human)

- Sniper (human)

- Medic

- Recon

Each has its own specialty and is better suited to certain situations. The difference between classes is subtle if you just choose on the first playthrough. And even more so if you get stuck and need to try out more characters.


As with all games of this type it's quite challenging to start with one class and then just play through to the end. After you get to a point where you're fairly comfortable, you'll want to play through that class until it's time to choose a new one.


It'll be a good challenge, especially because you'll have to be more careful than you often are in the original game. You'll have to manage your ammo, your health, and of course, your position:


- Behind cover - or at most a few meters (maybe less) out.

- Close up - you need to be close so you can be a target for enemies attacking you. Ideally you can get away from them by either crouching and shooting a shot down to one of the lower level's corners or by moving your body back in a circle until you either get into an open area or into the back of a truck, etc.

- In the open - it'll be hard to find a chance to shoot and survive from a vehicle, and you must do everything you can to stay hidden from other players. If you want to get away, you can either move as far away from them as you can and wait to be shot at by a player, or crawl away to where you think you can shoot before other players come and get you.

- As a Spy - it'll get harder and harder as time goes on to take down the enemies since there are no other players present, and no amount of aiming will save you, either. You need to be stealthy

America's biggest gun lobby is under fire for supporting a bill that allows any US citizen to bring a gun onto federal property.

The bill was introduced by the Republican chairman of the House, John Dingell, as part of a package dealing with new gun laws.

NRA spokesman Andrew Arulanandam said the bill complied with current laws under which all guns on federal land can be kept.

The bill has already been defeated by two House committees.

The NRA said earlier this year that Mr Dingell's bill would bring safety standards to the National Park Service.

But the Senate version of the gun control bill in early March included a provision that would have blocked the federal government from implementing a gun check system at parks that are under the responsibility of the states.

Mr Arulanandam has argued the NRA is "fully supportive of what the congressman and others are pushing for".

He told reporters on Tuesday that any legislation signed by Mr Dingell will also have to be passed by Congress and signed by President Barack Obama in order to become law.

He said the NRA's support of the bill, which the group opposed at the time, was "more in line with what we do", adding: "We are the only national firearm organisation that takes a position on what you would consider national parks. It has nothing to do with our stance in the debate over firearms".
